podcast.title: Most Downloaded Song on iTunes Opening Day
podcast.body: While it is impossible to determine the absolute first song downloaded from the iTunes Music Store on its opening day, January 9, 2001, due to tens of thousands of simultaneous users, U2's "Vertigo" emerged as the most downloaded song by the end of that day. This indicates its significant popularity at the launch of the digital music platform. "We do know that at the end of that first day, January 9th, 2001, this song from U2 was downloaded more than any other."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Ongoing History Book of Firsts

podcast.body: U2 partnered with Apple for the song "Vertigo" to leverage Apple's extensive marketing budget, ensuring the song's riff and The Edge's guitar were heard "everywhere" beyond just radio airplay. Bono justified these collaborations by stating his admiration for Apple's design, particularly Jony Ive's work on the iPod, and his belief that technology fundamentally changes music, citing examples like Jimi Hendrix's fuzz box and hip hop's use of samplers. He emphasized the band's intention to embrace technological advancements and market their music effectively. "We wanted to get that not just on the radio but everywhere. We wanted that riff. We wanted Edges guitar everywhere."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
